tiles.title: Binding request bodies to typed models

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Binding request bodies to typed models

blocks.text: Structured JSON bodies are distinct from URL inputs: path-declared parameters come from the path, ordinary scalars generally come from the query, and model parameters come from the body. One operation can receive all three.
Bind structured JSON by defining a BaseModel subclass and typing a handler parameter with that model.
FastAPI reads JSON, converts compatible values, validates the declared model, then gives the handler a model instance.

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Yield-based dependency cleanup

blocks.text: Acquire the resource before yield. The dependency supplies the yielded resource to the operation.
Surround yield with try/finally and release the resource in finally, covering successful use and exceptions.
Default request scope ends after response sending. Depends(provider, scope="function") ends after handler completion, before the response is sent.
If you catch an exception without intentionally handling it, re-raise it. Do not conceal the failure from FastAPI.

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: Trace acquisition, yield and operation use separately. Put release in finally so both successful and exceptional paths clean up. Default request scope ends after response sending; function scope ends after handler completion, before sending. If a caught exception was not intentionally handled, re-raise it. Yield is not a promise that every dependency ends at handler completion.

tiles.title: Structured service request and error logs

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Structured service request and error logs

blocks.text: An interpretable event log says when and where an event happened, its type and severity, and enough context to understand the outcome.
For a failure, use consistent field names for timestamp, application or code location, event type, severity, result status and reason—not just unexplained free text.

logger.error(message, extra=event_fields) attaches fields to the LogRecord. Configure the existing formatter or collector to preserve their names, and avoid custom keys that collide with reserved LogRecord attributes.

before.code:
import io
import logging
captured_output = io.StringIO()
logger = logging.getLogger('order.failure.exercise')
logger.handlers.clear()
logger.propagate = False
logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
existing_handler = logging.StreamHandler(captured_output)
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('%(message)s'))
logger.addHandler(existing_handler)
failure_values = {
    'timestamp': '2026-01-01T12:00:00Z',
    'code_location': 'orders.create_order',
    'event_type': 'order_failure',
    'event_severity': 'error',
    'result_status': 'failed',
    'reason': 'synthetic stock unavailable',
}
reserved_attributes = sorted(set(logging.makeLogRecord({}).__dict__) | {'message', 'asctime'})

logger.error('failed')
print(captured_output.getvalue(), end='')

after.code:

tiles.title: Preventing unsafe outbound requests and SSRF

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Preventing unsafe outbound requests and SSRF

blocks.text: For known destinations, map untrusted provider input to an allowed destination instead of accepting an arbitrary outbound URL.
For public-only access, reject private, loopback, link-local and other non-public addresses, including IPv6 equivalents.
Validate the resolved address actually used for the connection. Checking a hostname earlier is insufficient against a DNS rebinding gap.
Disable automatic redirects or enforce the same destination checks on every redirect target. An allowed starting URL can redirect somewhere forbidden.

tiles.title: Bounded form and multipart file inputs

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Bounded form and multipart file inputs

blocks.text: In one multipart handler, declare metadata with Annotated[Type, Form()] and the file with Annotated[UploadFile, File()]. Install python-multipart for parsing.
UploadFile uses a spooled file rather than requiring the entire upload as in-memory bytes. Its read, seek and close methods are asynchronous.
Set a finite RequestBodyLimitMiddleware max_body_size. Count actual incoming bytes, including multipart overhead; exceeding that limit returns 413.
request.form(max_files=..., max_fields=..., max_part_size=...) separately limits file count, field count and non-file field size. These limits do not replace the total-body limit.
Reject disallowed content types and validate fields before processing. When finished, release the upload with await file.close().
For this lab, disallowed attachment types use 415 and overlong metadata uses 422; total-body overflow uses 413. These are separate rejection conditions.

blocks.code:
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, File, UploadFile, HTTPException
from support import (RequestBodyLimitMiddleware, BoundedMultipartRoute,
                     budgets, permitted_content_types)
app = FastAPI()
app.router.route_class = BoundedMultipartRoute
app.add_middleware(RequestBodyLimitMiddleware,
                   max_body_size=budgets['max_body_size'])
@app.post('/orders/attachments')
async def attachment(metadata: Annotated[str, Form()],
                     file: Annotated[UploadFile, File()]):
    try:
        if file.content_type not in permitted_content_types:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail='disallowed content type')
        if len(metadata) > budgets['metadata_max_length']:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail='invalid metadata')
        data = await file.read(budgets['read_size'])
        await file.seek(0)
        return {'metadata': metadata}
    finally:
        await file.close()

annotations.text: Total actual-body-byte boundary, including multipart overhead.
Typed form metadata and spooled file; python-multipart required.
Asynchronous cleanup on success or rejection.

blocks.code:
from fastapi.routing import APIRoute
from support import budgets
class BoundedMultipartRoute(APIRoute):
    def get_route_handler(self):
        original = super().get_route_handler()
        async def bounded(request):
            # Parsing precedes automatic typed parameter binding.
            form = await request.form(max_files=budgets['max_files'],
                max_fields=budgets['max_fields'], max_part_size=budgets['max_part_size'])
            try:
                return await original(request)
            finally:
                await form.close()
        return bounded

annotations.text: Parser limits run before automatic typed parameter binding; non-file part size is separate from the total body budget.

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: Treat limits as separate controls. Form and File declarations need python-multipart; a spooled UploadFile offers asynchronous resource methods, not unlimited input. The finite body budget counts actual bytes including overhead and returns 413 on excess. Parser options bound file count, field count and non-file field size, but do not replace that budget. Validate fields and content type before processing, and close the file afterward.

steps.title: Declare the boundary: CORS origin and credential policy

blocks.text: Use app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...) with allow_origins, allow_methods, allow_headers and allow_credentials matching the browser client’s actual needs.
Defaults are restrictive: allowed methods default to GET, and credentials default to false.
With allow_credentials=True, specify origins, methods and headers explicitly rather than using wildcard lists.
CORS grants browser access permission; endpoint access-control checks remain separate and necessary.

blocks.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
app = FastAPI()
# Content-Type, and credentials; use explicit lists with no wildcards.
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=['https://shop.example'],
    allow_methods=['GET', 'POST'],
    allow_headers=['Content-Type'],
    allow_credentials=True)

annotations.text: Explicit shop-client permissions; credentials enabled. Browser permission does not replace endpoint access checks.

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: The shop browser needs its origin, methods and headers listed explicitly, with credentials enabled for this scenario. Defaults alone allow GET and leave credentials false. When credentials are true, do not use wildcard lists for origins, methods or headers. CORS answers a browser-permission question, not whether an endpoint should grant access. Keep endpoint access-control checks separate.

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Request-scoped dependency reuse and lifetime

blocks.text: FastAPI normally caches a dependency result within a request when several dependants declare the same dependency.
Use Depends(provider, use_cache=False) on a declaration that needs fresh execution instead of the cached result.
Check that two dependants receive the same provider result in one request, then examine a fresh request independently. This cache is request-local, not application-wide storage.

blocks.title: Separate request-cache boundaries
blocks.alt_text: Separate request-cache boundaries: Request A; Provider execution → value A; First dependant: same value A; Second dependant: same value A; Depends(provider, use_cache=False): fresh execution; Request B; Independent provider execution → value B; First dependant: value B; Second dependant: value B

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: Draw request A around its provider result and both dependants. Verify reuse inside that boundary, then inspect request B independently. On a declaration needing another execution, use Depends(provider, use_cache=False). The normal cache reduces repeat execution within one request; it does not turn a request-specific value into storage shared by all clients.

tiles.title: Required, optional and default input semantics · FastAPI OpenAPI generation from typed route contracts

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Required, optional and default input semantics

blocks.text: A default determines requiredness; a type that admits None determines nullability. These are different questions.
A nullable field with no default still requires presence. field: Type | None = None allows both omission and explicit null.
Send absence, explicit JSON null and a concrete value as separate requests. Compare each with the declared default and nullable type.

result_of.sql:
WITH inputs(ordinal, supplied, note) AS (VALUES (1,FALSE,NULL),(2,TRUE,NULL),(3,TRUE,'Leave at reception')), declarations(label, has_default) AS (VALUES ('note: str | None', FALSE), ('note: str | None = None', TRUE))
SELECT CASE WHEN NOT supplied THEN 'omitted' WHEN note IS NULL THEN 'explicit null' ELSE 'concrete string' END AS input,
 label AS declaration, (supplied OR has_default) AS accepted,
 CASE WHEN supplied OR has_default THEN note ELSE NULL END AS resulting_note
FROM orders CROSS JOIN inputs CROSS JOIN declarations ORDER BY ordinal, has_default

blocks.caption: Declaration comparison derived from the presence rule and supplied request bodies, not an HTTP run. Read resulting_note only where accepted is true.

blocks.text: Keep two columns in your mental model: must the field appear, and may its value be null? note: str | None requires presence but admits null. Adding = None allows omission too. Test missing, null and a concrete string separately against those declarations; “optional” alone does not identify both rules.

tiles.title: Credential and sensitive-data redaction from emitted logs

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Credential and sensitive-data redaction from emitted logs

blocks.text: Access tokens, passwords, primary secrets and sensitive personal data should usually not appear directly in logs. Remove or mask them under the logging policy.
Inspect supplemental context as well as the message: connection strings, session identifiers and other sensitive values can appear there.
Trigger a failure with recognizable synthetic sensitive values. Inspect emitted records to confirm prohibited values are removed while intended event fields remain.

before.code:
import io
import logging
class RedactingFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def __init__(self, secrets):
        super().__init__('%(message)s context=%(context)s event=%(event)s')
        self.secrets = secrets
    def format(self, record):
        text = super().format(record)
        for secret in self.secrets:
            text = text
        return text
def failure_harness(*, token, connection_string):
    output = io.StringIO()
    logger = logging.getLogger('order.redaction.exercise')
    logger.handlers.clear()
    logger.propagate = False
    logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(output)
    handler.setFormatter(RedactingFormatter([token, connection_string]))
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    logger.error('synthetic failure token=' + token, extra={
        'context': 'connection=' + connection_string + ' token=' + token,
        'event': 'order_failure'})
    text = output.getvalue()
    message, tail = text.rstrip('\n').split(' context=', 1)
    context, event = tail.rsplit(' event=', 1)
    return {'text': text, 'fields': {'event': event, 'context': context}}

result = failure_harness(token='FAKE_ORDER_TOKEN_ABC', connection_string='FAKE_CONNECTION_SECRET_XYZ')
print(result['text'], end='')

after.code:
import io
import logging
class RedactingFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def __init__(self, secrets):
        super().__init__('%(message)s context=%(context)s event=%(event)s')
        self.secrets = secrets
    def format(self, record):
        text = super().format(record)
        for secret in self.secrets:
            text = text.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')
        return text
def failure_harness(*, token, connection_string):
    output = io.StringIO()
    logger = logging.getLogger('order.redaction.exercise')
    logger.handlers.clear()
    logger.propagate = False
    logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(output)
    handler.setFormatter(RedactingFormatter([token, connection_string]))
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    logger.error('synthetic failure token=' + token, extra={
        'context': 'connection=' + connection_string + ' token=' + token,
        'event': 'order_failure'})
    text = output.getvalue()
    message, tail = text.rstrip('\n').split(' context=', 1)
    context, event = tail.rsplit(' event=', 1)
    return {'text': text, 'fields': {'event': event, 'context': context}}

result = failure_harness(token='FAKE_ORDER_TOKEN_ABC', connection_string='FAKE_CONNECTION_SECRET_XYZ')
print(result['text'], end='')

blocks.change_summary: Before: the same synthetic failure with masking disabled. After: policy masks prohibited strings throughout message and context while retaining the event field. Output is computed from this fixture.

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Request-scoped async-compatible PostgreSQL session lifecycle

blocks.text: AsyncSession holds mutable state for database work. It is unsafe to share across concurrent tasks; give each concurrent unit of work a separate session.
Bind async_sessionmaker to an async engine. async with session_factory() as session obtains and closes a session for the request’s unit of work.
A request dependency can yield the session from that async context. The context still owns cleanup on normal and exceptional exit.

blocks.title: One factory, separate concurrent sessions
blocks.alt_text: One factory, separate concurrent sessions: async_sessionmaker(async engine); Session A: mutable work state; Session B: mutable work state; Dependency yields session A; Dependency yields session B; async context exit closes A; async context exit closes B

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: Separate the engine-bound factory from the mutable sessions it creates. Concurrent request A and request B need separate sessions. Each request’s async context owns closure, including exceptional exit. Yield supplies the session to the operation without transferring that cleanup responsibility. A shared factory is not a shared AsyncSession.

steps.title: Work through the supplied example

blocks.text: Bind the factory to the async engine, then open a session with async with for each request’s work. Yield that session from inside the context so both normal and exceptional exit close it. Draw session A and session B separately for concurrent requests. Sharing factory setup does not permit both tasks to borrow one mutable session, and cleanup must not depend only on a successful return.

steps.title: Trace the contract

blocks.text: During a temporary required-backend outage, liveness can succeed while readiness removes traffic eligibility without requiring restart. Failed liveness can cause restart. HTTP statuses 200 through 399, including 3xx, mean success; an “unready” body does not override that status.

A YAML mapping uses `key: value`; a key with no value starts a nested mapping. Indent its children with spaces. For each probe, path and port are children of httpGet; periodSeconds and failureThreshold are siblings of httpGet. Edit only the YAML inside probe_yaml's triple quotes; the parser and service contract are supplied infrastructure.

blocks.code:
probe_yaml = """
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /live
    port: 8000
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8000
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 2
"""

annotations.text: Spaces nest httpGet under the probe, then path and port under httpGet.
Same indentation: periodSeconds and failureThreshold are siblings of httpGet.
The separate readiness mapping uses the same nesting and its supplied values.
